taxonomyNote: NatureServe: split from Mustela erminea by Colella et al. (2021) into M. erminea, M. richardsonii and M. haidarum. The ADW page read describes the pre-split M. erminea.
fieldMarks: Typical weasel form: long body, short legs, triangular head, round ears, long whiskers
Summer: chocolate-brown back with yellowish-white belly
Winter: white coat in northern animals, with a black tail tip
Tail about 35% of body length; males roughly twice the mass of females (ADW page for pre-split M. erminea)
behavior: Mainly nocturnal but frequently seen by day
Eats mainly small mammals, occasionally other small vertebrates and insects
In winter in southern Ontario, usually stayed beneath the snow surface
Dens in hollow logs, under stumps, roots, brush piles or rocks
habitat: Wooded areas with thick understory near watercourses; adapted to a wide variety of habitats and rarely in heavily forested regions.
range: Across Canada and south through most of the northern US to central California, northern Arizona, northern New Mexico, Iowa, the Great Lakes region, Pennsylvania and northern Virginia. Most of Alaska now refers to M. erminea.

lookalikes.name: Beringian ermine
lookalikes.howToTell: Same look; Alaska and western Yukon to Arctic Canada animals are M. erminea per NatureServe.

lookalikes.name: Least weasel
lookalikes.howToTell: Much smaller with no black tail tip.

lookalikes.name: Long-tailed weasel
lookalikes.howToTell: Larger, with a tail about half the body length.
